text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
ALITHIA
- Police could be examining the attempted murder of the baby found with needles in her body. Her parents plead ignorance.
- Right wing Disy expels party member who insists on standing as an independent candidate in Nicosia's Engomi suburb in next month's municipal elections.
- Increases in motor insurance premiums broke the law, says the finance ministry.
CYPRUS MAIL
- Chaos threatens as nurses warn of strikes in government hospitals.
- A three member panel appointed to investigate tender irregularities at the electricity authority is sworn in.
FINANCIAL MIRROR
- Sack EAC (electricity authority) bosses, says MP.
- Radio Shack, the U.S. consumer electronics retailer is due to open up stores in Cyprus before Christmas.
HARAVGHI
- Right-wing Disy seeks an alibi for its lack of democracy by expelling members who won't follow the party line.
- Police officers summoned colleagues from Paphos to Nicosia to tell them about a drugs squad raid, fearing the news could leak out to criminals if they told them over the telephone.
PHILELEPHTHEROS
- Municipal elections are the forerunner to presidential polls in 1998.
- Insurance companies deny they contravened the law by imposing higher rates for motor vehicle premiums.
SIMERINI
- 'Leave us alone!'. Father of little girl with needles in her body makes a dramatic appeal to the mass media.
- The Attorney-general will announce his decision today on whether policemen will be prosecuted in relation to crimes committed in Limassol last year.
